- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00) followed by a spike in news volume, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment declines sharply (e.g., -1.00) after a recent high, model often underreacts — adjust downward by 3–7% to align with mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (0.00–0.33) — add 2–5% bias upward for such periods.
- Forecast lag is common in early days of high sentiment — if sentiment rises >0.67 within 3–5 days, model should adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day.
- When news volume is high and sentiment is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce false peaks.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-stage momentum — if sentiment remains positive for 5+ days, add 1–2% incremental adjustment to final forecast.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume drops, model often holds too high — reduce forecast by 3–5% to reflect cooling sentiment.
